A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoRA-Ensemble research. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, support reliable comparison and matching across relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original image- and audio-classification experiments, computational measurements, and sensitivity analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds OOD detection, backbone-size experiments, and additional baseline evaluations.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the frozen backbone, member-specific low-rank attention updates, separately trained classification heads, and prediction averaging. Additional backbone tests and baseline adaptations do not change the proposed LoRA-Ensemble procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds near-OOD detection: models trained on CIFAR-100 distinguish CIFAR-100 samples from CIFAR-10 samples. This introduces a distinct uncertainty-detection task using existing datasets. CIFAR-10 classification was already present in v1 Appendix A.1; the original image, skin-lesion, and audio tasks remain.

E2.justification: Modified Snapshot Ensemble is newly evaluated on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and HAM10000. The new OOD comparison includes Split-Ensemble scores explicitly taken from Chen et al. (2024), rather than rerun. Appendix M separately reports an adapted FiLM-Ensemble trial. The original comparators remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include maximum-softmax OOD scoring with AUROC/AUPRC and HAM10000 evaluation using DeiT Tiny-16 and Small-16. Snapshot Ensemble introduces burn-in and cyclic training budgets, including 30 epochs for CIFAR. ESC-50 gains F1, NLL, and Brier evaluation; these metrics already existed for image tasks in v1's appendix.

E4.justification: v2 adds a distribution-shift detection test, an analysis of dependence on backbone size, and experiments examining FiLM-Ensemble adaptation difficulties. These substantially broaden the questions investigated. The original rank, initialization, injected-noise, and dropout sensitivity analyses remain under revised appendix labels.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five independent runs with different random initializations and one-sigma error bars. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure or significance test is introduced. Revised standard-deviation values and additional result rows do not change this reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds Snapshot, OOD, smaller-backbone, and FiLM results, plus ESC-50 F1/NLL/Brier scores. Its new OOD table reports LoRA-Ensemble AUROC/AUPRC of 82.1/84.1. Existing ESC-50 values also change: LoRA-Ensemble accuracy rises from 91.0 to 91.1 and ECE changes from 0.022 to 0.021. Existing image-classification scores are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix N.6–N.7 introduces mathematical definitions for the newly used AUROC and AUPRC metrics, including TPR/FPR and area integrals. Existing LoRA, initialization, and evaluation equations remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The introduction's contribution list and the conclusion extend the demonstrated application scope to OOD detection. The central claims about parameter-efficient transformer ensembling, calibration, and competitive predictive accuracy remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 extends the existing parameter-space explanation with backbone-size dependence, interprets the new near-OOD results, and discusses normalization difficulties for FiLM-Ensemble. ESC-50's calibration advantage is qualified as ECE-specific. The original limitations concerning diversity proofs, large-language-model evaluation, and computational complexity remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents Snapshot burn-in schedules, FiLM adaptation choices, and OOD confidence scoring. Conversely, Section 2.1 replaces v1's public code-and-weights statement and repository link with a future-release promise without the link. Core training hyperparameters, hardware, and runtime information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds OOD-related references to Chen et al., Sim et al., and Hendrycks and Gimpel, plus AUROC/AUPRC references. It expands discussion of existing implicit methods' transformer compatibility. The main related-work section and positioning relative to concurrent LoRA-ensemble research remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 5 becomes Discussion, incorporating an expanded calibration explanation while retaining limitations and future work. Experimental subsections and appendices are reorganized, and metric definitions receive separate headings. Most introduction, method, and related-work prose remains intact.

P2.justification: Separate CIFAR-100 and HAM10000 tables consolidate previously split main-text and appendix metrics. v2 expands the audio table, adds OOD, backbone-size, and FiLM tables, introduces HAM10000 diagnostic plots, and adds Snapshot curves to the CIFAR-100 figure. These substantially revise the result displays while retaining the original architectural and sensitivity figures.

improvement.justification: The new OOD and backbone experiments broaden empirical scrutiny. However, v2 Table 2 reports Snapshot Ensemble's CIFAR-100 Brier score as 1.614 at 77% accuracy, exceeding the conservative upper bound of 1.23 implied by the probability-based definition in Appendix N.5. The PDFs do not resolve this inconsistency. Its effect on the added comparison, together with removal of the code-and-weights link, prevents a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
